text:
On 2019-10-27, thirty-five of us said "abu bakr al-baghdadi," first entered that day by Bill Huizenga. Twenty-six of us said "isis leader abu," and twenty-four said "isis leader abu bakr al-baghdadi," both first entered by Ted Cruz. Twenty-five of us said "leader abu bakr al-baghdadi," also first from Ted Cruz. That single day, we converged.

By 2019-10-31 a different formation held. Twenty-five of us produced a "statement after voting"; twenty-five of us said "behind closed doors," first entered by John Barrasso. Twenty-one of us said "after voting against," and twenty of us said "statement after voting against," both first entered by Tim Walberg.

We record two peaks four days apart: one name we all reached for at once, and one procedural frame we returned to together. We were reading from the same page on both.
